policy.purpose: Challenge an already-independent executable Observatory frontier with authoritative public standards and primary research patterns that may expose missed architecture families or proof obligations.
policy.content_policy: The owner-signed manifest freezes source identity, status, version and challenge claims. It does not copy normative documents and does not claim that a standard proves the Observatory architecture.

sources.authority: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.status: latest ontology release identified by the official EU Vocabularies catalogue
load_bearing_claims: Legislation requires stable web identification and a common exchange data model usable by official publishers and other organisations.
The model separates FRBR-style legal resources and supports machine-readable cross-border metadata exchange.
A national canonical layer must interoperate without allowing the ELI projection to become a second writable truth seat.

sources.authority: Publications Office of the European Union
load_bearing_claims: Legal publication needs a formal model for analysing how modifying acts affect original or consolidated legislation.
The impact model extends beyond text replacement and can represent effects arising from court decisions.
A winning architecture must show whether its normative-effect calculus can project to ELI impact semantics without semantic loss.

sources.authority: Council of the European Union and Publications Office of the European Union
sources.version: Council Conclusions 2011/C 127/01 and current EUR-Lex implementation guidance
load_bearing_claims: Judicial decisions need uniform stable identifiers to support access, citation, search and linking across jurisdictions.
Case-law identity is not the same object as legislation identity or the version of legislation applicable to the decision.
A national Observatory must reconcile domestic identifiers and ECLI while retaining exact temporal links to authority versions.
Machine-readable legal documents require explicit structure, metadata and stable references to amendable substructures.
Document, expression and manifestation identity must not be collapsed.
Point-in-time consolidation and publication should be derivable from preserved structured legal content rather than maintained as an untraceable second corpus.
Legal identifiers should be meaningful, permanent and derived from invariant properties.
References commonly target precise hierarchical legal substructures and must remain stable across expressions and manifestations.
A canonical identity scheme must distinguish stable legal-object identity from version and content identity.
Legal rules carry temporal, deontic, authority and provenance annotations that cannot be represented as undifferentiated text.
A legal-rule representation should support normalization, external ontology references and linked-data mapping without making one serialization the canonical legal truth.
The Observatory effect model must show a deterministic, governed relationship between source evidence, rule interpretation and exchange projections.
Interoperable provenance needs explicit entities, activities, agents and qualified derivation relationships.
Domain-specific provenance may specialize a common model but must remain exchangeable and independently interpretable.
A winning architecture must prove that every public assertion can be reconstructed through preserved evidence and declared transformations.
RDF publication needs machine-checkable shape and constraint validation rather than schema claims by convention.
Graph constraints, target selection and validation results must be explicit and reproducible.
A linked-data projection must be validated as a projection of canonical state, not trusted as an independent authority store.
Append-only public logs require independently verifiable inclusion and consistency proofs, signed tree heads and explicit merge-delay behavior.
A log does not itself establish semantic correctness; monitors and admission criteria are separate responsibilities.
The Observatory must distinguish evidence transparency from canonical legal-effect computation and defend against split-view publication.

sources.status: latest stable 1.0 series identified by the official TUF specification index
load_bearing_claims: Long-lived trusted distribution needs role separation, threshold signatures, revocation, root continuity, rollback/freeze resistance and consistent snapshots.
The root of trust and delegated authority must evolve without relying on one permanently online key.
Observatory rule packs, schemas, releases and trust anchors need an explicit governed succession and recovery model.

sources.status: maintenance mode; official project recommends newer tiled-log approaches for new deployments
load_bearing_claims: A general transparency core must be separated from application-specific admission, canonicalization and external interfaces.
Scalable transparency can be multi-tenant and distributed while retaining inclusion and consistency proofs.
The Observatory should test whether transparency is a subordinate proof service, an authority seat or a dangerous conflation of the two.
Practical distributed systems can combine state-machine refinement with implementation verification to prove safety and liveness.
Testing a single-node substitute cannot establish the distributed claims of a replicated or sharded architecture.
A finalist whose genome relies on consensus, federation or distributed commit needs a machine-checkable model and an executable partition/fault campaign.
Crash correctness requires specifications that include crashes, recovery procedures and states at different abstraction layers.
Ordinary success tests do not prove recovery under arbitrary crash points.
An Observatory authority store must make crash/recovery obligations load-bearing and externally checkable.

sources.status: active research and mechanized proof framework
sources.version: current Perennial/Grove project line as of manifest date
load_bearing_claims: Concurrency, crashes, recovery and distributed-node failures can be verified in one program-logic framework.
A durable implementation and its recovery procedure must be related to the declared abstract state, not merely survive sampled tests.
A finalist claiming a tiny or verified trusted core must identify exactly which implementation/proof components remain trusted.
Crash-safety obligations may be enforced through a typed implementation discipline rather than a separate monolithic proof.
The architecture search must compare proof styles and trusted boundaries, not assume one formal-method family is universally superior.
A simpler compiler-enforced design is a valid challenger when it preserves the same measured legal and durability invariants.

sources.authority: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.status: latest version identified by the official EU Vocabularies catalogue
load_bearing_claims: Operational legal publication uses a formal ontology spanning official journals, legislation, case law, preparatory acts, expressions and manifestations.
A national architecture must account for multilingual and multiformat legal publication and institutional entities without copying the EU model as its canonical internal truth.
Interchange mappings must be versioned, testable and reversible.
